title: FAQ:
title_short: V08 · What Is the Universal Fund?
length: about 90 s (about 78 s with the optional lift)
headline: A small monthly gift goes to the next patient who is ready, and helps a hospital build for the next ten years: mpola mpola, slowly, slowly.
story: Mackinnon answers one question to camera: what is the Universal Fund? You give every month. Watsi sends it to the next patient who is ready. You get the update.

Then the story that makes it real: a partner hospital in Uganda that started as a shed under a jackfruit tree and grew into a maternal health center, on steady monthly giving. The word they use is mpola mpola. Warm, clear, hopeful. One person, one question, one ask.
do: Open on frame 1 with the question as top text. Cut out her own read of it.
Use one cutaway only: the real Universal Fund page on a phone.
Set “mpola mpola” in September Spirit over her shot. It is the line people remember.
dont: No full-screen title card for mpola mpola.
No Medellín B-roll over the Uganda story.
No more than one brand element on screen at a time.
Do not post the same week as V03 (the jackfruit story repeats).

bp_intro: All source times are in Mincho5153.MP4 (1:40, one 4K camera, Mackinnon only). Times come from the word-level transcript.json and are accurate to about 0.2 s. Find exact in and out points on the waveform. Every frame is from the real file. The yellow box shows the 9:16 crop.

rows.frame_alt: Mackinnon seated by big windows, city behind, grey Watsi T-shirt
rows.visual: Mackinnon, wide and locked-off. In-point on “Watsi's”. Cut out her own read of the question (00:01.10–00:05.80). The text replaces it.
rows.motion: Question on top from frame 1, top third: What is the Universal Fund? Lato Bold, Watsi yellow #FFCC33, soft shadow. Cut on. It doubles as the thumbnail. Stays to 00:05.5. Captions start with her voice.

voice.quote: Watsi's Universal Fund is how we support people who want to give consistently, but don't want to pick a specific patient each time.

rows.music: Music enters under her first word. Warm, sustained piano or guitar bed, 18–20 dB under her voice. No drums.

rows.visual: Same shot. Keep her small pause before “And”.
rows.motion: Question fades out at 00:05.5 (6 frames). Name super “Mackinnon” at 00:06.5–00:08.5, lower left, above the captions, large. First name only.

voice.quote: So here's how it works. And it's actually one of the very best ways you can help on Watsi.

rows.visual: Stay on her for “You sign up… any time.” Then the one cutaway of this video, from “Each month” (00:24.90): a screen recording of the real watsi.org/universal-fund page on a phone. Record it fresh. Never fake a page. Back on her face for “when their care is complete.”
rows.motion: Captions only. Write “$5” with the dollar sign.

voice.quote: You sign up for a monthly donation, it can start with simply $5 and you can cancel or change it at any time. Each month, that money goes directly to a new patient in need. You get an update on who you helped, and you hear how they're doing when their care is complete.

rows.sfx: One soft UI tap on the cut to the phone. Nothing else.

rows.visual: On her. Slow 2% push-in across the line. Keep the breath before “To patients who are waiting”.

voice.quote: You're not choosing who, but you're trusting us to direct your donation each month to where it is needed the most. To patients who are waiting, whose care is ready to happen, whose families have been hoping someone will simply say yes.

rows.visual: Back to 100%. Hard cut. Optional lift: if V1 runs over 80 s, drop this whole row first.

voice.quote: Over time, you become part of a community. We have donors who've been in our Universal Fund for even a decade. They've helped sometimes now hundreds of patients across dozens of countries.

rows.frame_alt: Mackinnon gesturing as she tells the Uganda story
rows.visual: On her the whole time. There is no Uganda footage in this shoot. Do not use Medellín B-roll as Uganda. One 106% punch-in on “One of our partner hospitals in Uganda” to mark the story.

voice.quote: And that steady, reliable giving is also what helps Watsi and our medical partners plan. Here's what I mean. One of our partner hospitals in Uganda, it simply started as a shed under a jackfruit tree, giving away malaria medicine. And then over more than a decade, built on this kind of consistent support from our Universal Fund, it has now become a new maternal health center.

rows.music: Small lift on “maternal health center”. Not a swell.

rows.frame_alt: Mackinnon, hands together at her chest
rows.visual: Back to 100% on “The word”. Let her say it. No freeze, no full-screen card.
rows.motion: Brand touch (the only one): mpola mpola in September Spirit, Watsi yellow, top third, on her shot, timed to her voice. Holds 2 s after she says it. Caption reads “mpola mpola”. The transcript says “Mopola Mopola”: that is wrong.

voice.quote: The word they use is mpola mpola, slowly, slowly.

rows.visual: On her. Hold 0.7 s after “look”, then cut to the end card.

voice.quote: And that's what your monthly gift is really doing. It's not just one surgery. It's the reason a hospital can build for the next 10 years. Your monthly donation goes incredibly far, and it's a lot bigger than it can sometimes look.

rows.music: Gentle peak on “bigger”. Resolve on the cut.

rows.visual: Clean end card. Light cyan #D3EDFA background. Navy is never a background.
rows.motion: watsi.org/universal-fund, all lowercase, Lato, navy #2E2844. One line. Nothing under it. No stats, no donate button.

Uppbeat, like other Watsi cuts. Save the license certificate with the project: YouTube flagged an Uppbeat track on a Watsi upload on 7 Oct.
tech: 3840×2160, 23.976 fps, H.264, 2-ch audio recorded into the camera
1080×1920 at 23.976 fps. Same as the source. No frame-rate change.
A 9:16 crop of 4K is 1215×2160, so it is sharper than 1080×1920. Punch-ins up to 112% stay native. The room is dim: lift exposure and skin a little, keep it natural.
2 channels recorded into the camera. Pick the live channel on the waveform and map it to both sides. Mute the other. (Not measured: the Drive download limit stopped the audio check.)
Lato Bold, white, soft shadow, large. Pop word by word. No highlight box, no shading block. One line at a time. Always on screen, also in pauses. Keep the bottom 20% clear for app buttons.
Record watsi.org/universal-fund on a real phone, vertical, 1080×1920 or larger. No fake UI.
checklist: Read every caption against the audio. Sonam checks every word, and typos are her top complaint.
The transcript writes “WOTC”. It is Watsi, capital W only. The URL is watsi.org, all lowercase.
The question is on screen from frame 1 and stays at least 5 seconds.
Name super “Mackinnon” is large, first name only, and never at 0:00.
Captions never drop out, even in pauses.
“mpola mpola” is lowercase, two words, both in the caption and the September Spirit text.
End card reads watsi.org/universal-fund, lowercase, nothing under it.
client_note: Why this matters: Sonam asked for the question typed on screen first, so the first frame tells you what the video is about. The Universal Fund is Watsi's main ask. Make it easy to understand.
